audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Zophar's first speech: accusation of many words, claim that Job receives less than guilt deserves, unreachable divine wisdom, call to repent, and restoration promise. Marked as Zophar's speech, not final theology.

verses.restored: Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:

familiar.text: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

modern.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

original.text: וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Should a multitude of words go unanswered, and should a man of lips be justified?

familiar.text: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?

modern.text: “Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?

original.text: הֲרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֵעָנֶ֑ה וְאִם אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפָתַ֣יִם יִצְדָּֽק

verses.restored: Should your empty talk make people silent, and when you mock, shall no one shame you?

familiar.text: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

modern.text: Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?

original.text: בַּ֭דֶּיךָ מְתִ֣ים יַחֲרִ֑ישׁו וַ֝תִּלְעַ֗ג וְאֵ֣ין מַכְלִֽם

verses.restored: For you say, My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes.

familiar.text: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.

modern.text: You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’

original.text: וַ֭תֹּאמֶר זַ֣ךְ לִקְחִ֑י וּ֝בַ֗ר הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: But if only the Divine would speak and open his lips with you,

familiar.text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;

modern.text: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,

original.text: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם מִֽי יִתֵּ֣ן אֱל֣וֹהַּ דַּבֵּ֑ר וְיִפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתָ֣יו עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: and tell you secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom is double-sided. Know then that the Divine lets some of your guilt be forgotten for you.

familiar.text: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

modern.text: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.

original.text: וְיַגֶּד לְךָ֨ תַּֽעֲלֻמ֣וֹת חָכְמָה֮ כִּֽי כִפְלַ֪יִם לְֽת֫וּשִׁיָּ֥ה וְדַ֡ע כִּֽי יַשֶּׁ֥ה לְךָ֥ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵעֲוֺנֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Can you find out the deep things of the Divine? Can you find out the limit of Shaddai?

familiar.text: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

modern.text: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?

original.text: הַחֵ֣קֶר אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּמְצָ֑א אִ֤ם עַד תַּכְלִ֖ית שַׁדַּ֣י תִּמְצָֽא

verses.restored: It is higher than heavens; what can you do? Deeper than Sheol; what can you know?

familiar.text: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

modern.text: They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol—what can you know?

original.text: גָּבְהֵ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם מַה תִּפְעָ֑ל עֲמֻקָּ֥ה מִ֝שְּׁא֗וֹל מַה תֵּדָֽע

verses.restored: Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.

familiar.text: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

modern.text: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.

original.text: אֲרֻכָּ֣ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִדָּ֑הּ וּ֝רְחָבָ֗ה מִנִּי יָֽם

verses.restored: If he passes through, imprisons, and calls an assembly, who can turn him back?

familiar.text: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?

modern.text: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?

original.text: אִם יַחֲלֹ֥ף וְיַסְגִּ֑יר וְ֝יַקְהִ֗יל וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: For he knows worthless people; he sees harm, and will he not consider it?

familiar.text: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?

modern.text: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?

original.text: כִּי ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע מְתֵי שָׁ֑וְא וַיַּרְא אָ֝֗וֶן וְלֹ֣א יִתְבּוֹנָֽן

verses.restored: An empty-headed person may get heart, when a wild donkey's colt is born human.

familiar.text: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.

modern.text: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!

original.text: וְאִ֣ישׁ נָ֭בוּב יִלָּבֵ֑ב וְעַ֥יִר פֶּ֝֗רֶא אָדָ֥ם יִוָּלֵֽד

verses.restored: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward him,

familiar.text: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

modern.text: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,

original.text: אִם אַ֭תָּ֗ה הֲכִינ֣וֹתָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֖ אֵלָ֣יו כַּפֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: if harm is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice dwell in your tents,

familiar.text: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

modern.text: if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,

original.text: אִם אָ֣וֶן בְּ֭יָדְךָ הַרְחִיקֵ֑הוּ וְאַל תַּשְׁכֵּ֖ן בְּאֹהָלֶ֣יךָ עַוְלָֽה

verses.restored: then you will lift your face without blemish; you will be firm and not fear.

familiar.text: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

modern.text: then indeed you will lift up your face without shame; you will stand firm and unafraid.

original.text: כִּי אָ֤ז תִּשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֣יךָ מִמּ֑וּם וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֻ֝צָ֗ק וְלֹ֣א תִירָֽא

verses.restored: For you will forget trouble; like waters that have passed by, you will remember it.

familiar.text: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:

modern.text: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.

original.text: כִּי אַ֭תָּה עָמָ֣ל תִּשְׁכָּ֑ח כְּמַ֖יִם עָבְר֣וּ תִזְכֹּֽר

verses.restored: Your life will rise brighter than noon; darkness will become like morning.

familiar.text: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday: thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

modern.text: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.

original.text: וּֽ֭מִצָּהֳרַיִם יָק֣וּם חָ֑לֶד תָּ֝עֻ֗פָה כַּבֹּ֥קֶר תִּהְיֶֽה

verses.restored: You will be secure because there is hope; you will look around and lie down in safety.

familiar.text: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.

modern.text: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.

original.text: וּֽ֭בָטַחְתָּ כִּי יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝חָפַרְתָּ֗ לָבֶ֥טַח תִּשְׁכָּֽב

verses.restored: You will lie down, and none will make you tremble; many will seek your favor.

familiar.text: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

modern.text: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.

original.text: וְֽ֭רָבַצְתָּ וְאֵ֣ין מַחֲרִ֑יד וְחִלּ֖וּ פָנֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים

verses.restored: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; escape will perish from them, and their hope will be the breathing out of life.

familiar.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.

modern.text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”

original.text: וְעֵינֵ֥י רְשָׁעִ֗ים תִּ֫כְלֶ֥ינָה וּ֭מָנוֹס אָבַ֣ד מִנְהֶ֑ם וְ֝תִקְוָתָ֗ם מַֽפַּח נָֽפֶשׁ
